answer: The lantern multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and cipher lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3218 identities would post 1195 proofs and burn roughly 14 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
